requirement:
Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.

```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
```
rationale:
**Obligations from `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.mcp`:**
1. `get_next_page` takes one `uuid` argument, and the result is an object.
2. The caller passes the `next` UUID exactly as the previous page returned it.
3. That UUID identifies the prepared result and so determines the shape of the returned object.

Other behavior is delegated to sibling requirements. `pages.behavior` covers reuse, malformed or unknown UUIDs, and page contents. `pages.inputs` covers dependencies. `pages.mcp.description` covers the tool description. None of these needs a test here.

**Mapping to tests:**
- **Tool signature.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` asserts that the `get_next_page` tool is exposed. It asserts the exact parameter schema `{type: object, required: [uuid], properties: {uuid: {type: string, format: uuid}}}`.
- **Passing `next` unchanged, with the shape following the UUID.** Each test below feeds the returned `next` value straight into `get_next_page` as `{"uuid": next}`. Each then asserts the shape of the returned object:
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` returns a search page with `matches`, `search_id` and no `instructions`. It also asserts that the page's `matches[0]` carries the later hit's node.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items]` returns outline pages with `node` and `items`. It returns node-read pages with `text`, `children`, `file` and `selector`.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]` returns listing pages with `files`, each entry having `node` and `data`.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation]` returns a text page of the form `{text, next}` from a `read_node` continuation. The harness replaces the scripted `use_next` with the real returned UUID, and the following page's `next` is checked to be a valid, different UUID.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` is not part of this mapping. It covers only the schema.
- The same tests cover several different result kinds (search, outline, node-read, listing and text reads). Together they show that one `get_next_page` tool returns different object shapes depending only on the UUID.

**Gaps:** I found none. The remaining behaviors (invalid, unknown and other-conversation UUIDs, reuse, snapshots, dependencies) belong to sibling requirements. The tests also exercise them, for example the invalid and unknown UUID errors in the outline test.

text: :::{req} pages.mcp
Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.
```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
:::{req} pages.behavior
Each page has the same result fields as the originating tool. Text reads return
successive portions of text. Listings, outlines, and searches return successive
arrays of whole entries in their original order. Only a page with a successor
includes `next`.
Reusing a UUID returns the same page from the original snapshot, including the
same successor UUID if more remains. A malformed UUID, an unknown UUID, or a UUID
from another conversation returns a tool error under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.tool_agent.isolation`.
:::{req} pages.inputs
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
:::{req} pages.mcp.description
> `Pass the UUID from next to read the next page in the same format. When next
> is absent, this is the last page.`
